title: Garden-Based Learning as a Sustainability-Oriented Approach: Perspectives of Prospective Social Studies Teachers
content: Garden-based learning (GBL) connects sustainability education with experiential and place-based learning. This study examined prospective social studies teachers’ attitudes toward GBL and their views of its benefits, limitations, and implementation. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was used with students at Afyon Kocatepe University during the 2025–2026 academic year. Quantitative data were collected from 100 participants using the Attitude Scale toward the Garden-Based Learning Approach, and qualitative data were obtained from semi-structured interviews with 24 participants. After normality was confirmed, independent-samples t-tests and one-way analysis of variance were conducted at α = 0.05; interview data were analyzed through content analysis. Attitudes were generally high. No statistically significant gender differences were observed, whereas grade level and sensitivity to environmental problems produced significant differences. Qualitative findings indicated that GBL supports experiential and lasting learning, environmental awareness, holistic development, motivation, and social interaction. Participants also identified constraints related to infrastructure, climate, teacher competence, finance, safety, and time, and proposed infrastructure improvements, training, funding partnerships, stronger safety measures, and technology integration. The findings suggest that GBL can strengthen sustainability-oriented social studies teacher education when institutional and practical barriers are addressed.
